clue.text: Sleeping on the streets in support of aristocrat

parts.note: someone out is outdoors, on the streets rather than at home
for means in support of, and a count is a European aristocrat

explanation.surface: A campaigner sleeps rough in solidarity with a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests homelessness; in fact the phrase means knocked unconscious, as a boxer who fails to rise before the referee counts to ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a boxer floored for ten seconds is unconscious, and the phrase is used loosely of anyone deeply asleep.

clue.text: Polar feature (and creature) in present incumbent

indicators.note: in says the two pieces sit within the word for present

parts.note: to offer is to present
ice is a feature of the polar regions
a bear, here a polar one

explanation.surface: An Arctic feature and its famous animal are found in a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polar' does double service: polar ice and polar bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who currently holds a post is its incumbent.

clue.text: The curtain rising over a lull in hostilities

indicators.note: rising says the hidden letters are read backwards
over as in spanning: the letters wanted stretch over the boundary between the two words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The theatre curtain goes up after a break in fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'over', but 'over' signals the letters straddling The curtain; the definition is the lull alone. 'rising' reads ECURT upwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an agreed ceasefire is a pause in fighting.

clue.text: Somehow prove it hurts the Queen to conquer

indicators.note: somehow suggests an unspecified rearrangement of the letters of prove

parts.note: ow is the cry when something hurts
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to prove it pains the Queen to be defeated.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to overcome by superior strength is to conquer.

clue.text: Bather unexpectedly catching cold is a sign of cancer

indicators.note: catching says the abbreviation is enclosed by the shuffled letters
unexpectedly suggests the letters of bather turn up in a new order

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A swimmer who catches a chill is showing a symptom of disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cancer' is the zodiac sign, not the illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrology: the zodiac sign Cancer is represented by a crab.

clue.text: Biannual event is mostly horse and bull

indicators.note: mostly says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: equine means relating to horses
an ox is a bovine animal, loosely a bull

explanation.surface: A twice-yearly show is largely horses and bulls.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: day and night are equal twice a year, in March and September.

clue.text: Pledges to serve cereal in hospital? On the contrary!

indicators.note: on the contrary reverses the surface order, so the hospital goes into the cereal

parts.note: oats are a cereal crop
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A promise to serve porridge in a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says cereal in hospital; 'On the contrary!' swaps the roles, putting H inside OATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: solemn promises or vows are pledges.

clue.text: Should one engage with errand to attend literacy class?

definitions.text: Should one engage with errand to attend literacy class?

indicators.note: engage with suggests the two words mesh together like gears, so their letters intermingle

explanation.surface: Should someone running an errand drop in on a reading lesson?
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ONE and ERRAND mesh to give the answer; the whole clue describes who a literacy class serves.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a person unable to read is the one a literacy class is designed for.

clue.text: Worm's bit of good luck

definitions.meaning: a parasitic flatworm, such as the liver parasite of sheep

explanation.surface: A worm enjoys a stroke of fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Two unrelated senses: a parasitic flatworm, and a chance success, both spelt the same.

clue.text: Delighted with next July: it's pants without clothes!

indicators.note: each word is stripped of its outer covering, its first and last letters, leaving only the inner ones

explanation.surface: Someone is thrilled that next July they can go about without trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without clothes' tells you to strip each of next, July, it's and pants of its first and last letters: EX, UL, T, ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone exultant is triumphantly joyful, overjoyed.

clue.text: Sally sitting around, motionless

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Sally sits about, not moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone keeping put without moving is motionless.

clue.text: Nice expensive copy inside — not so expensive

indicators.note: inside says the word for copy sits within the French word

parts.note: in Nice, a French city, the word for expensive is cher
to ape is to copy or imitate

explanation.surface: A costly replica on the Riviera turns out to be a bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the adjective but is the French Riviera city, so 'expensive' is to be translated into French.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of cheap: something cheaper costs less, so is not so expensive.

clue.text: Finally, mountain climb is beginning

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word mountain

parts.note: an ascent is a climb up a slope

explanation.surface: At last the mountain ascent is starting.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something nascent is just coming into being, at its start.

clue.text: Where flies are unfair

definitions.meaning: trouser flies sit beneath the waistband
a blow beneath the waist is illegal in boxing, hence unsporting

explanation.surface: A question about where insects gather, with a complaint of injustice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flies' are not insects but the zip opening of trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal position under the waistband for flies, and the boxing rule against low punches for the idiom meaning unsporting.

clue.text: Thrice adrift?

parts.note: the answer means adrift three times over: its first word, its last two words, and the whole phrase each mean adrift

explanation.surface: A boat drifts away for the third time.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition in disguise: LOST, AT SEA and the full phrase all mean adrift.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym, tripled: being lost, being at sea and being lost at sea all describe drifting helplessly.

clue.text: St Stephen's lower, discarded greeting

parts.note: a lower is one that lows, an ox; discarded means binned, so the ox is put in the bin, giving B-OX-IN
g'day is the Australian greeting

explanation.surface: A saint's cow and a rejected hello, oddly listed together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' means one that lows, not 'less high'. 'discarded' does double duty: binned, so the ox goes in the bin. St Stephen's Day, 26 December, is the British public holiday after Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Calendar equivalence: the feast of St Stephen falls on 26 December, the British holiday after Christmas.

clue.text: Derelict and remote cathedral

indicators.note: derelict means fallen into ruin, so the letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A ruined, isolated cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the famous Gothic cathedral on the Île de la Cité in Paris.

clue.text: Spongy clue for boars?

parts.note: the letters ABSOR, when bent, that is rearranged, become the word boars

explanation.surface: A request for a clue to pigs that are somehow spongy.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as ABSOR BENT, an instruction to scramble ABSOR, which gives BOARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a spongy material soaks up liquid readily.

clue.text: Young female or male caught up in tangled web

indicators.note: in says the reversed word sits inside the tangled letters
tangled says the letters of web are knotted into a new order
caught up says the word male is turned upward, read backwards in a down light

explanation.surface: A young creature of either sex is trapped in a messy web.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tangled' turns WEB into EW…B; 'caught up' reverses MALE to ELAM, which goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Farming term: a female sheep in her first year is a young female.

clue.text: See 13
Capturing part of the city

indicators.note: part of says only a portion of the word Capturing is wanted

explanation.surface: An army seizes a section of the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an Italian city in Piedmont, home of the famous shroud.

clue.text: Cancellation period definite

parts.note: an era is a period of history
sure means certain or definite

explanation.surface: A definite deadline for calling something off.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: rubbing out or deleting a record is a form of cancellation.

clue.text: Guest argues regularly as a matter of habit

indicators.note: regularly says to take every other letter, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A visitor habitually picks fights.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: customary practice, the way things are habitually done.

clue.text: Grants immunity to plotter, primarily involved in Semtex explosion

indicators.note: involved in says that letter is wrapped inside the rest
an explosion blows the letters of Semtex apart into a new order
primarily picks out the leading letter of plotter

explanation.surface: A bomb plotter is let off after a Semtex blast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosion' turns SEMTEX into EXEMTS; 'involved in' puts P from 'plotter, primarily' into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to exempt someone is to free them from a duty or liability, granting immunity.

clue.text: Call that's mostly fraudulent

indicators.note: mostly says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: phoney means fake or fraudulent

explanation.surface: A scam call.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to call someone is to ring them up on the telephone.

clue.text: In dunce's cap, a delinquent frolic

indicators.note: In says the answer is held within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A naughty child in the dunce's cap misbehaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a prank or wild adventure, a bit of mischievous fun.

clue.text: Premium oil mixed in this?

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, premium, with the 1 read as the letter I

indicators.note: mixed says the letters of oil are stirred together in a new order

explanation.surface: Top-quality oil blended into something, presumably a sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' points to the whole clue: a sauce made by mixing oil in. A1 becomes AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Allusive: garlic mayonnaise is made by whisking oil into egg yolk, so it is a thing with premium oil mixed in.

clue.text: Finally, Dilys and Victor in a bed, cavorting — perhaps they'll be given a last-minute reprieve

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the name Dilys
cavorting suggests prancing about, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the words they'll be are a loose arrangement to be reordered

explanation.surface: Dilys and Victor romp in bed, presumably hoping for a timely interruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cavorting' mixes S, V and A BED into SAVEDB; 'perhaps' turns THEY'LL BE into YTHEBELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom from boxing: a fighter about to lose is rescued when the round ends, so escaping at the last moment.
